blocks.text:
In the morning, the yacht anchors off Floreana in the southern part of the archipelago. After breakfast, you will make a wet landing at Punta Cormorant, beside a large brackish lagoon. Greater flamingos, ducks, black-necked stilts and other shorebirds can be seen here. Sea turtles nest on the beaches at night, while rays and sharks may be spotted close to shore.

After returning to the yacht, you can go kayaking or head to Devil’s Crown for snorkelling. Devil’s Crown is a volcanic crater almost entirely submerged beneath the sea. Only a small crown-shaped ridge remains above the surface. Coral reefs and a rich variety of marine life thrive below the water, while seabirds gather in the open sea.

After lunch featuring Ecuadorian cuisine with Andean influences, continue to Post Office Bay. Drop a letter in its famous mailbox and take part in a tradition begun by whalers centuries ago. You will also see a building once used by a fishing company in the 1920s.

The next stop is the Baroness Lookout on northern Floreana. Your guide will recount the island’s mysterious story of a baroness, murder and enduring legends.

Back on board, dinner pairs Japanese techniques with Peruvian seasonings, featuring fresh local fish and seafood. On a clear night, enjoy a cocktail on the upper deck beneath the stars of both hemispheres.
